analysis_notes.source_text_summary: Torah #284 (LM1) is a single-paragraph teaching. Rebbe Nachman rebukes a person who claims he has no time for Torah due to business obligations. He rules that one must in any case 'snatch' (לַחֲטֹף) some time for Torah study daily. He then interprets the Talmudic phrase 'Did you set times for Torah?' (Shabbat 31a) — the word 'keva' (קֶבַע) carries the meaning of robbery (גְּזֵלָה), as in the verse 've-kava et koveihem nefesh' (Proverbs 22:23). Thus the question means: did you rob/steal time from your business and devote it to Torah? The entire teaching is one sustained exhortation with one supporting word-study. No conceptual network of bechina (parallel-nature) relationships is developed.
